Species: dogs

Additional details: "Used to assess the integrity of the blood-brain barrier."
Reported evidence: Evans blue dye was injected i.v. to assess the integrity of the blood-brain barrier; after 20 min, no dye was observed in the brain, CSF, and brain IF, although the remainder of the body and viscera was intensely colored.

Result: 2 %
Assay context: pharmacokinetics
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: permeable

Additional details: "CSF concentrations were similar to those found in brain tissue."
Reported evidence: In a pharmacokinetic study of CRA, brain concentrations were about 2% of those in plasma. The ability of CRA to cross the blood–brain barrier was evidenced by the fact that its CSF concentrations were similar to those found in brain tissue.

Result: impermeable BBB permeability

Additional details: "No radioactivity was detected in the brain for either the parent compound or its metabolites."
Reported evidence: In studies involving male and female rats, no radioactivity was found in the brain at any time, showing that neither Carmoisine nor its metabolites cross the blood-brain barrier.

Evidence family: direct_brain_exposure
Endpoint: Kp
Result: 0.76 ratio
Assay context: in vivo
Species: FVB mice
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: good_penetration
  - bbb_transport_label: not_subject_to_efflux

Additional details: "1 mg/kg IV dose, measured at 5 min; negligible in vivo P-gp efflux measured."
Reported evidence: In wild-type FVB mice, compound 14 showed good to excellent CNS penetration at 5 min following a 1 mg/kg IV dose, with a brain concentration to plasma concentration ratio (Kp) of 0.76. Negligible in vivo P-gp efflux was also measured.

Result: permeable BBB permeability
Species: rat
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: permeable

Additional details: "Brain tissue levels measured via HPLC showed OKN-007 was taken up by both normal brain and tumor tissue equally following oral administration."
Reported evidence: OKN-007 is a small molecule that crosses the BBB. In rats, high performance liquid chromatography-derived brain tissue levels demonstrated that OKN-007 was taken up by both normal brain and tumor tissue equally following oral administration.

Evidence family: direct_brain_exposure
Endpoint: concentration in the brain
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: in vivo
Species: mice
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: poor_penetration

Additional details: "Baseline control group given water."
Reported evidence: Sulphanilic acid normally penetrates the brain in only very small amounts. In mice, concentrations of sulphanilic acid in the brain under control conditions (water) were measured at 0.84, 0.29, and 0.30 mg per 100 g brain.

Evidence family: direct_brain_exposure

Result: permeable BBB permeability
Assay context: CSF measurement
Species: human
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: permeable

Additional details: "Measured approximately 4-5 hours after the day 10 dose; absolute CSF concentrations were 87.8 and 24.4 ng/mL."
Reported evidence: BIT225 was measured in CSF in two patients at ~4-5 h after the day 10 dose. CSF concentrations were 87.8 and 24.4 ng/mL and the respective CSF/plasma ratios were 2.5 and 1.5%, indicating that BIT225 penetrates the blood-brain barrier.

Endpoint: total exposure in rat brain tissues
Result: 0.0234 µM h
Assay context: 10 mg/kg oral administration
Species: rat
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: poor_penetration

Reported evidence: Following 10 mg/kg oral administration of amitraz in rats, amitraz showed a low brain-to-plasma distribution ratio and a total brain tissue exposure of 0.0234 µM*hr.

Evidence family: direct_brain_exposure
Result: permeable BBB permeability
Assay context: intravenous administration
Species: rat
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: permeable

Additional details: "Compound was detected in the brain."
Reported evidence: Urolithin B was detected in the brain of rats upon intravenous administration, confirming that this compound can cross the blood brain barrier.

Reported evidence: A recent study demonstrated that NXY-059 had poor brain uptake in animals subjected to transient focal ischemia.

Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy

Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Conditions: "physiologic conditions"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: restricted

Additional details: "The dye strongly binds to albumin, and this complex is impermeable to the BBB."
Reported evidence: Under physiologic conditions, the blood-brain barrier (BBB) is impermeable to macromolecules such as albumin. Because Evans Blue (EB) dye binds strongly to albumin, it remains restricted within the blood circulation and cannot cross the barrier.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7731
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: in situ brain examination
Species: goldfish
Conditions: "except for some special areas such as the anterior and posterior choroid plexus and the saccus vasculosus"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: poor_penetration

Additional details: "1% dye solution used."
Reported evidence: Examination of the brains in situ 4 hr after injection of 1% trypan blue in goldfish yielded the finding that these dyes are confined to the blood vessels except for some special areas such as the anterior and posterior choroid plexus and the saccus vasculosus.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.8179
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: intravenous injection
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Reported evidence: Max Goldmann showed that while trypan blue injected into the lumbar subarachnoid space stained the CNS, intravenous injections stained the body but not the nervous system.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7549
Result: increased_permeability
Assay context: intraventricular injection of collagenase
Species: rat
Conditions: "BBB permeability increased reversibly by proteolytic enzymes (specifically collagenase) acting on basement membrane collagen"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: increased_permeability

Reported evidence: Intraventricularly injected collagenase and other proteolytic enzymes are able to reversibly increase the permeability of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) to different tracers such as trypan blue in rats.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.81
Result: increased_permeability
Assay context: Pentschew and Garro model
Species: rat
Conditions: "severe disruption of the blood-brain barrier associated with high-dose lead-induced encephalopathy"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: increased_permeability

Additional details: "Trypan blue was used as an extracellular tracer."
Reported evidence: In the Pentschew and Garro model involving high doses that produce encephalopathy, there is a severe disruption of the blood-brain barrier to extracellular tracers such as trypan blue.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.8234
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Species: human
Conditions: "normal conditions (non-anoxic)"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Additional details: "Based on studies of human fetuses."
Reported evidence: Based on Gröntoft's work on human fetuses, it is necessary for the brain to be anoxic to permit a trypan blue infiltration into the brain tissue, implying it is impermeable under normal conditions.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.8248
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Species: human, rat
Conditions: "foetuses"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: poor_penetration

Reported evidence: In human and rat foetuses, no significant penetration of trypan blue into the brain was observed.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.8114
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: carotid artery injection
Species: guinea pig
Conditions: "control animals (plasma injection only)"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Additional details: "The barrier in the neocortex remained intact."
Reported evidence: In matched control guinea pigs injected with plasma only, the blood-brain barrier in the neocortex remained intact and did not show extravasation of trypan blue.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.823
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Species: dog
Conditions: "brain temperature of 13° C and higher"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Reported evidence: The blood-brain barrier of the new-born pup was found to withstand hypothermic brain temperatures of 13-16° C without passing trypan blue, remaining efficient at 13° C and higher.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7933
Result: increased_permeability
Assay context: vital staining
Conditions: "Specific brain regions with sinusoidal blood vessels, including area postrema, hypothalamus, choroid plexus, dura, hypophysis, tuber cinereum, paraphysis, pineal gland, and preoptic recess"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: increased_permeability

Additional details: "Compound: trypan blue."
Reported evidence: Regions such as the area postrema and hypothalamus, as well as the choroid plexus, dura, hypophysis, tuber cinereum, paraphysis, pineal gland, and preoptic recess, have been credited with increased permeability of the blood-brain barrier to trypan blue due to the sinusoidal blood vessels characteristic of these areas.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.803
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: animal experiments
Conditions: "intravenous injection"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Reported evidence: In animal experiments, it was shown that after intravenous injection of trypan blue, all tissues with the exception of the brain and the spinal cord were colored, demonstrating that the blood-brain barrier is impermeable to the dye.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.8103
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: in vivo
Conditions: "water-intoxicated animals"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Additional details: "administered parenterally"
Reported evidence: In water-intoxicated animals, the blood-brain barrier is intact, as evidenced by the fact that parenterally administered trypan blue does not penetrate into the brain.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.83
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: in vivo injection
Species: mice, rats
Conditions: "dye-protein complexes"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: restricted

Additional details: "Staining was observed in CVOs and the choroid plexus; no accumulation of dye was observed in neurons with projections beyond the BBB."
Reported evidence: In neonatal and adult mice and rats injected with 1-2% Trypan blue, staining was restricted to the vessels of the brain and the circumventricular organs (CVOs), including the choroid plexus of all ventricles.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.8178
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: in vivo injection
Species: dogs and rabbits
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: poor_penetration

Reported evidence: Experiments in dogs and rabbits showed that while intravenous injection of the acidic dye Trypan blue stained the whole animal, the brain and spinal cord remained unstained.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.8269
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Species: cats, rabbits and rats
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Reported evidence: In experiments with cats, rabbits and rats, it was shown that the brain vessel wall is impermeable to trypan blue.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7355
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: tracer permeability method
Species: rat
Conditions: "normal condition"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Reported evidence: Trypan blue is identified as a tracer that does not pass the blood-brain barrier (BBB) under normal conditions, although gross spots of staining were observed in the brain stem and hypothalamus after 20–60 Gy irradiation.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7904
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: IV injection vs spinal cavity injection
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Reported evidence: Goldmann observed that while intravenous injection of Trypan blue did not result in brain staining or toxicity, direct injection into the spinal cavity caused convulsions, paralysis, and deep blue staining of the brain, leading to the conclusion that a barrier exists between the blood and brain tissue that does not let Trypan blue pass.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7984
Result: increased_permeability
Assay context: macroscopic observation
Conditions: "Urokon (sodium acetrizoate) damage"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: increased_permeability

Reported evidence: Macroscopic observations of trypan blue patterns showed that Urokon-damaged brains usually exhibited a confluent staining pattern, indicating dye penetration.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.8199
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Species: guinea pig
Conditions: "lead poisoned"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Reported evidence: Trypan blue fails to enter the brain of lead poisoned guinea-pigs.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.6604
Result: increased_permeability
Assay context: ligation of the common carotid artery followed by exposure to an environmental pO2 of 30 mm Hg
Species: rat
Conditions: "alteration of the blood-brain barrier caused by ischemia"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: increased_permeability

Additional details: "Extravasation of trypan blue was directly correlated with increased brain water content."
Reported evidence: In rats, after ligation of the common carotid artery and exposure to an environmental pO2 of 30 mm Hg, a direct correlation was found between increased cerebral water content and the amount of extravasated trypan blue, which was attributed to an alteration of the blood-brain barrier caused by ischemia.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.8255
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: intravenous administration
Species: dog
Conditions: "cerebral hypothermia (brain temperature 8-27.8° C), tested 18-76 days post-hypothermia"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Reported evidence: Four dogs subjected to cerebral hypothermia (lowest brain temperature 8° C., highest 27.8° C.) were given 1% trypan blue intravenously; none of these brains were blue at sacrifice (18 to 76 days post-hypothermia), suggesting no immediate or delayed disturbance of the barrier.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.8283
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Species: mouse
Conditions: "adult mouse"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Reported evidence: Dyes, such as trypan blue, injected into the circulation, are not taken up by the brain of the adult mouse.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7706
Result: increased_permeability
Species: dog
Conditions: "BBB injury following resuscitation (open-chest cardiac compression method)"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: increased_permeability

Reported evidence: In a study using Trypan blue as a BBB tracer, extravasation of the dye was found in 3 of 7 resuscitated dogs.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.8297
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Species: rat
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Reported evidence: Trypan blue is described as a tracer that does not normally penetrate the blood-brain barrier.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7496
Result: increased_permeability
Assay context: in vivo and supravital experiments
Conditions: "air embolism causing BBB damage"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: increased_permeability

Additional details: "Invasion of trypan blue into vascular wall structures occurs after exposure to air embolism for only a few seconds, while extra-vascular staining requires about 6-7 minutes of exposure."
Reported evidence: The results confirm that air embolism, in vivo as well as supravitaly, causes a BBB damage as indicated by abnormal permeation of trypan blue.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7696
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: inspection of the removed brain
Species: rabbit
Conditions: "normal barrier conditions"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: poor_penetration

Additional details: "Trypan blue is used to demonstrate the existence or absence of barrier alteration."
Reported evidence: Trypan blue is unable to pass from blood to brain under normal barrier conditions and shows a marked tissue affinity and poor diffusibility.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.8044
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: i.v. injection
Species: laboratory animals
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Reported evidence: In laboratory animals, intravenous injection of dyes such as trypan blue colored all tissues except the brain, demonstrating that the dye does not cross the blood-brain barrier.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7975
Result: increased_permeability
Assay context: visual evidence
Conditions: "intracarotid injections of serotonin (3.65 to 6.15 mg)"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: increased_permeability

Additional details: "The increased permeability was typically observed on the side of injection only, although one case showed generalized permeability."
Reported evidence: In five experiments, clear-cut visual evidence of increased permeability of the cerebral vascular bed to trypan blue was observed after total intracarotid injections of serotonin varying from 3.65 to 6.15 mg.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.8259
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Species: rabbit
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Reported evidence: BROMAN & OLSSON (1948) developed a method in the rabbit using trypan blue, which will not normally leak through the blood-brain barrier, as an indicator to demonstrate lesions.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7577
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: intravenous injection
Species: albino mice
Conditions: "bound to albumin"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Additional details: "penetration occurs only after opening of the BBB"
Reported evidence: Trypan blue, bound to albumin and administered intravenously to albino mice, escapes to the brain parenchyma only after the opening of the blood brain barrier (BBB).

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7467
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: histological observation
Species: dog
Conditions: "control group (intact BBB)"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Additional details: "The 1% trypan blue was administered via intravenous drip for 30 to 40 minutes prior to slaughter."
Reported evidence: In the control group of dogs, there was no leakage of the pigment (trypan blue) into the brainstem, and histological examination showed no extravasation of the pigment from the arteries, veins, and capillaries of the brainstem.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7569
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: dye penetration assay
Species: rat
Conditions: "sham-operated (intact spinal cord BBB)"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Reported evidence: No trypan blue dye penetration was noted at any postoperative time in the spinal cord of sham-operated animals.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7861
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: embryonic chick/quail transplant model
Species: chick/quail
Conditions: "embryonic chick brain transplanted to embryonic quail gut"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Additional details: "Exclusion of trypan blue was noted as a typical biochemical and morphological feature of the BBB in this model."
Reported evidence: In experiments where embryonic chick brain was transplanted into embryonic quail gut, the resulting brain transplant was vascularized by vessels of gut origin that exhibited typical BBB features, including the exclusion of trypan blue.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7598
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: CEC in vitro
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Additional details: "Used as a marker for albumin."
Reported evidence: The impermeability of brain microvessel endothelial cell (CEC) monolayers in vitro for trypan blue, a marker for albumin, was demonstrated.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.762
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: intraperitoneal injection
Species: rat, mouse
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Reported evidence: Trypan blue injected intraperitoneally did not stain the brain, an indication that the blood brain barrier was intact as far as trypan blue was concerned.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.7832
Result: impermeable BBB permeability
Assay context: fluorescence microscope
Species: rabbit
Conditions: "control hemisphere"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: impermeable

Additional details: "Fluorescence was observed only within the blood vessels, with no extravascular fluorescence."
Reported evidence: In the cortex from the control hemisphere of a cold lesion, no specific fluorescence of either trypan blue or catecholamines can be seen outside the vessels.

Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy

Result: increased_permeability
Assay context: in vivo
Species: mouse
Conditions: "infected brain; development of a 'leak' in the capillary endothelium beginning on the 3rd day of infection"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: increased_permeability

Additional details: "The increase in permeability caused the brains to become progressively bluer as the dye fixed in brain cells."
Reported evidence: Experiments with Pontamine sky blue in infected mice indicated the development of a 'leak' in the capillary endothelium beginning on the 3rd day, resulting in the brains becoming progressively bluer until death on the 6th day.

Level: L2
Evidence family: central_functional_access_proxy
Transfer likelihood: 0.5015
Result: increased_permeability
Species: mice
Conditions: "breakdown of the blood-brain barrier"
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: increased_permeability

Additional details: "Marked leakage of Pontamine blue was used to demonstrate the breakdown of the blood-brain barrier."
Reported evidence: The breakdown of the blood-brain barrier in both actively and passively protected mice is demonstrated by the marked leakage of Pontamine blue and γ-globulins.

SMILES: Cc1cc(-c2ccc(N/N=C3\C=Cc4c(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])c(N)c4C3=O)c(C)c2)ccc1N/N=C1\C=Cc2c(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])c(N)c2C1=O.[Na+].[Na+].[Na+].[Na+]
Morgan similarity: 0.2857

Evidence family: passive_permeability
Transfer likelihood: 0.796
Endpoint: leakage
Result: ~2-fold increase
Assay context: intravenous injection
Species: mouse
Conditions: "DR6 knockout adult mice"
Additional details: "The observed leakage was similar in magnitude to barrier deficits seen after intracortical delivery of VEGF."
Reported evidence: Adult DR6 knockout mice exhibited an approximately 2-fold increase in Evans blue dye leakage compared to wild-type littermate controls following intravenous injection.

SMILES: C=CC(=O)Nc1cc(C)cc(-n2c(=O)ccc3cnc4cc(-c5ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc5)ccc4c32)c1
Morgan similarity: 0.1778

Level: L3
Evidence family: passive_permeability
Transfer likelihood: 0.064
Endpoint: permeability
Result: 28.5 %
Assay context: in vitro HBEC-5i cell model
Experimental details:
  - bbb_permeability_label: permeable

Additional details: "Measured at 24 h; permeability was attributed to be lower than ibrutinib due to higher retention rates of JS25 in the cells."
Reported evidence: JS25 effectively crosses the blood-brain barrier, showing a permeability of 28.5% in an in vitro HBEC-5i cell model at 24 h.
